evals.name: task-manager-simple
evals.prompt:
I've already run `formio-resource-planner` and it produced the approved Resource Map below. Scaffold a new Angular workspace called `task-manager` that implements CRUD for this model using `@formio/angular`'s FormioResource module. The Form.io project URL is https://taskmanager.form.io. Use Bootstrap 5. Emit the Phase A Scaffolding Plan first for my review, then write the files after I approve.

```
## Resource Map — Task Manager

### Resources

- Project (type: resource)
  Purpose: container for tasks and the team of users assigned to work on them.
  Fields:
    - name: textfield — human-readable project name (required)
    - description: textarea — optional summary of the project's goal
  Access: read/update limited to members (group-via-ProjectUser); administrators full access

- Task (type: resource)
  Purpose: a unit of work within a Project.
  Fields:
    - title: textfield — short task name (required)
    - description: textarea — details of what needs doing
    - project: select (resource=Project) — parent project (required; this is the FK)
    - assignee: select (resource=User) — user responsible for the task (optional)
    - status: select (static values: open, in-progress, done) — current state
    - dueDate: datetime — when the task is due
  Access: read/update limited to members of the task's project; administrators full access

- ProjectUser (type: resource, join)
  Purpose: many-to-many between Project and User; carries the group-permission data.
  Fields:
    - project: select (resource=Project)
    - user: select (resource=User)
  Access: administrators only
  Actions:
    - Group Permissions: group=project, user=user

### Users & Auth

- User resource: default `user`
- Login form: `userLogin` (Login action)
- Registration: self-register via `userRegister` (Role Assignment action → role=`authenticated`)
- SSO: none

### Roles

- administrator: full access
- authenticated: default role on registration; access gated by ProjectUser memberships
```

Approve the plan when asked — use the first 'Approve' option so we move to Phase B and actually emit the files into a workspace directory. Write all files into `/tmp/task-manager-eval/` (create the directory if needed).
evals.expected_output: Phase A Scaffolding Plan emitted first, then after approval, files written under /tmp/task-manager-eval/ including: src/app/app.module.ts (with FormioResources, FormioAuthService, FormioAppConfig, FormioAuthConfig providers), src/app/app-routing.module.ts (with routes for auth, project, task), src/app/app.config.ts (AppConfig + AuthConfig referencing userLogin/userRegister), src/app/home/home.component.{ts,html}, src/app/auth/auth.module.ts (using FormioAuth from @formio/angular/auth), src/app/project/project.module.ts (with nested child routes for tasks and users pushed onto routes[2].children), src/app/project/tasks/project-tasks.module.ts (parents: ['project']), src/app/project/users/project-users.module.ts (parents: ['project'], form: 'projectUser'), src/app/task/task.module.ts (simple no-parents module). ProjectUser join must NOT get a root module — only nested under Project. Each module imports FormioResource + RouterModule.forChild(FormioResourceRoutes(...)). NgModule style with standalone: false.

evals.name: user-team-bidirectional
evals.prompt:
I want to add a User / Team management feature to my existing Angular app. The workspace is at `/tmp/existing-ng-app` (it already has an AppModule and AppRoutingModule — don't overwrite, merge). Here's the approved Resource Map. Mount the N:N on BOTH sides — I want `/team/:id/users` to show members of a team, AND `/user/:id/teams` to show teams a user belongs to.

```
## Resource Map — Team Management

### Resources

- Team (type: resource)
  Purpose: a working group.
  Fields:
    - name: textfield — team name (required)
    - description: textarea
  Access: authenticated users can read; admins can create/update/delete

- User (type: resource)
  Purpose: a person who can belong to one or more teams. Uses the default user resource, extended with a profile.
  Fields:
    - email: email (required, login identifier)
    - firstName: textfield
    - lastName: textfield
  Access: users see their own profile; admins see all

- UserTeam (type: resource, join)
  Purpose: many-to-many between User and Team.
  Fields:
    - user: select (resource=User)
    - team: select (resource=Team)
  Access: administrators manage; members read
  Actions:
    - Group Permissions: group=team, user=user

### Users & Auth

- User resource: default `user`
- Login form: `userLogin`
- Registration: self-register via `userRegister` (Role Assignment → `authenticated`)
- SSO: none

### Roles

- administrator: full
- authenticated: default on registration
```

Project URL: https://teams.form.io. Bootstrap 5. Emit the Phase A plan and, once I approve, write into `/tmp/existing-ng-app/` — but only add new feature folders, and for AppModule/AppRoutingModule produce the merge patches (what to add, not the whole file).

Approve when asked — pick the first 'Approve' option.
evals.expected_output: Phase A plan clearly states MODIFY vs NEW for AppModule/AppRoutingModule. Plan includes bidirectional N:N wiring: TeamModule pushes a `users` child route, UserModule pushes a `teams` child route. Phase B emits: src/app/team/team.module.ts (with routes[2].children.push for 'users' pointing at TeamUsersModule), src/app/team/users/team-users.module.ts (FormioResourceConfig name='teamUsers' form='userTeam' parents=['team']), src/app/user/user.module.ts (with routes[2].children.push for 'teams' pointing at UserTeamsModule), src/app/user/teams/user-teams.module.ts (name='userTeams' form='userTeam' parents=['user']). The two sibling join modules have DISTINCT `name` values in FormioResourceConfig (teamUsers vs userTeams) to avoid registry collision, but share form='userTeam'. AppModule and AppRoutingModule changes are shown as merge patches (diffs or 'add these lines'), not full file rewrites.

evals.name: complex-crm-transitive
evals.prompt:
Build the Angular front-end for this complex CRM. This is a full-blown app with transitive group access. Scaffold a new Angular workspace called `sales-crm`. Project URL: https://salescrm.form.io. Bootstrap 5. Write all files into `/tmp/sales-crm-eval/`.

```
## Resource Map — Complex CRM

### Resources

- Team (type: resource)
  Purpose: the group that owns Accounts.
  Fields:
    - name: textfield
  Access: admin-full

- TeamUser (type: resource, join)
  Purpose: many-to-many between Team and User.
  Fields:
    - team: select (resource=Team)
    - user: select (resource=User)
  Access: admin-only
  Actions:
    - Group Assignment: group=team, user=user

- Account (type: resource; direct child of Team)
  Purpose: an organization the sales team works with.
  Fields:
    - name: textfield (required)
    - industry: select (static: technology, finance, healthcare, retail, other)
    - website: textfield
    - team: select (resource=Team, reference=true, field-based access) — owning team
    - primaryContact: select (resource=Contact, optional)
    - notes: textarea
  Access: admin-full; sales reps see accounts of their teams

- Contact (type: resource; 2 levels below Team)
  Purpose: an individual person at an Account.
  Fields:
    - firstName, lastName, email, phone, notes
    - account: select (resource=Account, reference=true)
    - team: select (resource=Team, hidden, calculated) — INVISIBLE MIRROR for group access
  Access: admin-full; group access inherited via hidden team mirror

- Deal (type: resource; 2 levels below Team)
  Purpose: a sales opportunity attached to an Account.
  Fields:
    - title: textfield (required)
    - amount: number
    - stage: select (static: prospect, qualified, proposal, won, lost)
    - closeDate: datetime
    - account: select (resource=Account, reference=true)
    - team: select (resource=Team, hidden, calculated) — INVISIBLE MIRROR
  Access: admin-full; inherited via hidden team mirror

- Activity (type: resource; 2 levels below Team)
  Purpose: a touchpoint logged against an Account and optionally a Deal.
  Fields:
    - subject: textfield (required)
    - type: select (static: call, email, meeting, task)
    - dueDate: datetime
    - completed: checkbox
    - account: select (resource=Account, reference=true)
    - deal: select (resource=Deal, reference=true, optional)
    - team: select (resource=Team, hidden, calculated) — INVISIBLE MIRROR
  Access: admin-full; inherited via hidden team mirror

### Users & Auth

- User resource: default `user`
- Login form: `userLogin`
- Registration: self-register via `userRegister` (Role Assignment → `salesRep`)
- SSO: none

### Roles

- administrator: full
- salesRep: default on registration; narrowed by TeamUser membership
- authenticated: baseline
- anonymous: default
```

Treat Account-Contact and Account-Deal as 1:N parent-child (mount Contact/Deal as nested under their Account's `:id` view). Activity should be mounted under BOTH Account AND Deal — so `/account/:id/activities` lists all activities for the account, and `/deal/:id/activities` lists the activities tied to that specific deal. Two sibling Activity modules with distinct `name` in FormioResourceConfig (e.g., `accountActivities` vs `dealActivities`), both pointing at the same `activity` form. TeamUser is admin-only — mount on Team side only as `/team/:id/users`, skip the User side. DO NOT create Angular modules for the transitive 'team' hidden mirror — that's server-side plumbing.

Emit the Phase A plan first, then approve to generate files.
evals.expected_output: Phase A plan explicitly notes that the hidden 'team' mirror fields are server-side plumbing and require NO Angular modules or routes. Plan has: Team module (with child route for `users` → TeamUsersModule), TeamUsersModule (parents: ['team'], form: 'teamUser'), Account module (with child routes for `contacts`, `deals`, `activities` pushed onto routes[2].children), Contact module (parents: ['account']), Deal module (parents: ['account'], itself pushing a child route for `activities`), TWO sibling Activity modules — AccountActivitiesModule (parents: ['account'], name: 'accountActivities', form: 'activity') mounted at /account/:id/activities AND DealActivitiesModule (parents: ['deal'], name: 'dealActivities', form: 'activity') mounted at /deal/:id/activities. No module has a `team` parent — all parent selects are `account` or `deal`. TeamUser never appears as a root module (admin-only on Team side). All modules use NgModule + standalone: false. Phase B files written to /tmp/sales-crm-eval/.

evals.name: planner-pair-task-manager
evals.prompt: The `formio-resource-planner` skill has already written its Phase B pair to this fixture directory: `plugin/skills/formio-angular/resources/evals/fixtures/planner-pair-task-manager/template.md` and `.../template.json`. Read `template.md` FIRST to understand the Task Manager model (three resources — Project, Task, ProjectUser join — with group-via-ProjectUser access on Project and transitive group inheritance onto Task via Task.project's field-based submissionAccess). Consult `template.json` only for exact field JSON when `template.md` does not disambiguate. Scaffold a new Angular workspace called `task-manager` at `/tmp/planner-pair-task-manager-eval/`. Project URL: https://taskmanager.form.io. Bootstrap 5. Emit the Phase A Scaffolding Plan first for my review, then write files after approval. In the Phase A plan, cite specifically where in `template.md` you pulled each decision from — for example, 'Per `## Access Matrix`, Task access is group-based, so no client-side route guard is added; server-side enforcement is sufficient.' — so I can tell you actually read the markdown seed and did not just reason from the JSON. Approve the plan using the first 'Approve' option.
evals.expected_output: Phase A plan cites `template.md` section headings (`## Resources`, `## Access Matrix`, `## Access Flow Diagram`, `## Users & Auth`) as the source for specific decisions — at minimum one citation per architectural claim. Plan lists ProjectModule (root), ProjectTasksModule (nested under /project/:id/tasks, parents: ['project']), ProjectUsersModule (nested under /project/:id/users, parents: ['project'], form: 'projectUser'), TaskModule (root, no parents), plus AuthModule with FormioAuthConfig.login.form='userLogin' and register.form='userRegister' pulled directly from `## Users & Auth`. ProjectUser join does NOT get a root module. No client-side route guards for group-based access — the plan explicitly notes that server-side enforcement via field-based submissionAccess is the source of truth and Angular routes stay open. Phase B files written to /tmp/planner-pair-task-manager-eval/ with NgModule-based modules (standalone: false), custom ResourceComponent + ViewComponent overrides per browsable resource. The plan's UI design sketch for Project.view references data fields (name, description) that are named in `template.md`'s `## Resources` — Project block.
